<?php

function isLeap($year) {
    if (($year % 4 == 0 && $year % 100 != 0) || $year % 400 == 0) {
        return 29;
    } else {
        return 28;
    }
}

function no_of_days_remaining($mon, $year) {
    $days = 0;
    switch ($mon) {
        case 1: $days += 31;
        case 2: $days += isLeap($year);
        case 3: $days += 31;
        case 4: $days += 30;
        case 5: $days += 31;
        case 6: $days += 30;
        case 7: $days += 31;
        case 8: $days += 31;
        case 9: $days += 30;
        case 10: $days += 31;
        case 11: $days += 30;
        case 12: $days += 31;
    }
    return $days;
}

function no_of_days_passed($mon, $year) {
    $days = 0;
    switch ($mon) {
        case 12: $days += 31;
        case 11: $days += 30;
        case 10: $days += 31;
        case 9: $days += 30;
        case 8: $days += 31;
        case 7: $days += 31;
        case 6: $days += 30;
        case 5: $days += 31;
        case 4: $days += 30;
        case 3: $days += 31;
        case 2: $days += isLeap($year);
        case 1: $days += 31;
    }
    return $days;
}

function no_of_days($year) {
    return 31 * 7 + 30 * 4 + isLeap($year);
}

$input1 = trim(fgets(STDIN));
$input2 = trim(fgets(STDIN));

list($yy1, $mm1, $dd1) = array_map('intval', explode(':', $input1));
list($yy2, $mm2, $dd2) = array_map('intval', explode(':', $input2));

if ($yy2 > $yy1) {
    $m1 = $mm1; $y1 = $yy1; $d1 = $dd1;
    $m2 = $mm2; $y2 = $yy2; $d2 = $dd2;
} else {
    $m1 = $mm2; $y1 = $yy2; $d1 = $dd2;
    $m2 = $mm1; $y2 = $yy1; $d2 = $dd1;
}

$nodA = no_of_days_remaining($m1, $y1);
$nodC = no_of_days_passed($m2 - 1, $y2);

if ($yy2 > $yy1) {
    $start = $yy1;
    $end = $yy2;
} else {
    $start = $yy2;
    $end = $yy1;
}

$nodB = 0;
for ($i = $y1 + 1; $i <= $y2 - 1; $i++) {
    $nodB += no_of_days($i);
}

$nod = ($nodA - $d1 + 1) + ($nodC + $d2) + $nodB - 1;

if ($yy1 == $yy2) {
    if ($mm2 > $mm1) {
        $nod = (no_of_days_remaining($mm1, $yy1) - $dd1 + 1) - (no_of_days_remaining($mm2, $yy2) - $dd2 + 1);
    } else if ($mm2 < $mm1) {
        $nod = (no_of_days_remaining($mm2, $yy2) - $dd2 + 1) - (no_of_days_remaining($mm1, $yy1) - $dd1 + 1);
    } else {
        if ($dd1 > $dd2) {
            $nod = $dd1 - $dd2;
        } else {
            $nod = $dd2 - $dd1;
        }
    }
}

echo $nod;

source_data.prob_desc_description: Calendars in widespread use today include the Gregorian calendar, which is the de facto international standard, and is used almost everywhere in the world for civil purposes. The Gregorian reform modified the Julian calendar's scheme of leap years as follows: Every year that is exactly divisible by four is a leap year, except for years that are exactly divisible by 100; the centurial years that are exactly divisible by 400 are still leap years. For example, the year 1900 is not a leap year; the year 2000 is a leap year.   In this problem, you have been given two dates and your task is to calculate how many days are between them. Note, that leap years have unusual number of days in February.Look at the sample to understand what borders are included in the aswer.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first two lines contain two dates, each date is in the format yyyy:mm:dd (1900 ≤ yyyy ≤ 2038 and yyyy:mm:dd is a legal date).
